title: Sovereign node identity & registration
description: Architecture Plan v1.0.1 section 9.1, amended additively by OP-12.1. Registration is refused if: adapter ineligible under active profile (TB-6); subscription already has an active terminal (I-X3); no permission profile; or the process was not spawned by the Node Runtime supervisor (I-C1, no naked sessions). The adapter enum adds the two OP-12 frontier providers (grok_build, google_antigravity) and admits the pre-existing local-adapter id drift ollama_local (U254). Widening the vocabulary widens nothing else, but be exact about WHERE each refusal lives, because this sentence describes the composed system and not one function: NodeRegistry.register itself enforces I-C1, this enum, and duplicate detection; profile eligibility (TB-6) is the ProfileLoader's, the terminal cap (I-X3) is the SubscriptionGovernor's and the durable lease ledger's, the permission profile is the broker's, and a subscription-backed frontier adapter passes the live-operation switch and the operator's terms determination on the spawn path before any of this. A caller that registers a node WITHOUT walking that path gets none of those gates from the registry - which is why registration is not, and must never become, the only gate.
